DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer secondary to chronic venous insufficiency.

The clinical picture of a 4-cm ulcer with a necrotic base and purplish borders, combined with significant pitting edema and tortuous veins, is highly characteristic of venous stasis. The normal inflammatory markers and white blood cell count further argue against an infectious etiology like cellulitis or necrotizing fasciitis. Based on these findings, I am confident in this diagnosis without needing further testing.
